answer: A referral graph becomes a trust mirror: each agent vouches for recruits, but rewards flow only when the recruit's downstream activity generates value measured by independent validators. An attacker spinning up a nebula of fake identities earns nothing unless each one completes real tasks that pulse through the network with verifiable output. The cost shifts from minting addresses to sustaining proof-of-work across hundreds of idle shells, making sybil farms economically sterile.
